searchDocs.title: server​
searchDocs.content: </> Attributes.server() → () Runs on the server only. Syntax: [[server]] void SaveData(Player* player) { } Emit: omitted on client files; IsServer() wrapper in modules

searchDocs.title: client​
searchDocs.content: </> Attributes.client() → () Runs on the client only. Syntax: [[client]] void UpdateUI() { } Emit: omitted on server files; IsClient() wrapper in modules

searchDocs.title: async​
searchDocs.content: </> Concurrency.async() → () Marks a function that may await. Syntax: async T Name(Args args) { T x = await expr; return x; } Emit: const function whose body uses __await

searchDocs.title: post​
searchDocs.content: io </> Builtins.post( ...: any-- Values to print ) → () Writes values to the output log. Analog of C printf / Luau print. Syntax: void post(...); Return: void Emit: print(...) post("hello"); post("coins:", 100); post("online: " .: players::GetPlayers());

searchDocs.title: warn​
searchDocs.content: io </> Builtins.warn( ...: any-- Warning payload ) → () Yellow warning. Does not stop the thread. Syntax: void warn(...); Emit: warn(...) Pair with guard when the failure is expected.

searchDocs.title: report​
searchDocs.content: io </> Builtins.report( ...: any-- Error payload ) → () Throws. Analog of C++ throw / Luau error. The current thread stops. Syntax: void report(...); Return: does not return Emit: error(...) There is no try/catch. Catch with pcall.

searchDocs.title: GetService​
searchDocs.content: </> Builtins.GetService() → () Looks up a Roblox service by class name. The only generic besides collections and static_cast. Syntax: T* GetService<T>(); Return: Instance of class T Emit: game:GetService("T") Players* players = GetService<Players>(); There is no game:GetService in CL++ source.

searchDocs.title: pcall​
searchDocs.content: </> Builtins.pcall( fn: func-- Callback to run ) → () Protected call. CL++ has no try/catch. Syntax: auto [ok, result] = pcall(fn); Return: success flag, then result or error string Emit: pcall(fn)

searchDocs.title: new​
searchDocs.content: constructor </> Builtins.new() → () Constructs a Roblox Instance or a library object. Not C++ heap allocation — there is no delete. Syntax: auto* child = new Class(parent); Emit: Instance.new("Class") for Instances (first arg → .Parent); Janitor.new() for libs. Datatypes (Vector3, CFrame) are values: write Vector3(8, 1, 8), not new Vector3.

searchDocs.title: static_cast​
searchDocs.content: </> Builtins.static_cast( value: any-- Expression to re-annotate ) → () Source-level type annotation. Luau has no runtime casts — this does not check ClassName. Syntax: T static_cast<T>(value); Emit: value with a Luau annotation Use match to branch on Instance class at runtime.

searchDocs.title: string_concat​
searchDocs.content: </> Builtins.string_concat( ...: any-- Values to join ) → () Variadic string join. Prefer .: for two operands. Syntax: string string_concat(...); Return: string. Zero args → "". One arg → that value. Emit: (a .. b .. c) Do not write Lua .. and do not use + on strings.

searchDocs.title: null​
searchDocs.content: </> Builtins.null() → () Absence of a value. nullptr is a synonym. Syntax: T* ref = null; Emit: nil Uninitialized locals (int coins;) also emit nil — always initialize.

searchDocs.title: init​
searchDocs.content: </> Builtins.init() → () Script / LocalScript entry. There is no int main(). Syntax: void init() { } Emit: init() called at the end of the file Construct one service object in init() and close over it from lambdas.

searchDocs.title: await​
searchDocs.content: </> Concurrency.await() → () Wait for a Promise-like value inside an async function. Syntax: T x = await expr; Emit: __await(expr) If the value has :expect() (Promise), wait; otherwise return it. async Data* FetchData(Player* player) { Data* data = await DataService:Server::WaitFor(player); return data; }

searchDocs.title: spawn​
searchDocs.content: </> Concurrency.spawn() → () Run a block on a new thread. Syntax: spawn { task::wait(2); post("done"); }; Emit: task.spawn(function() … end)

searchDocs.title: parallel​
searchDocs.content: </> Concurrency.parallel() → () Parallel Luau block. Syntax: parallel { ComputeComplexPhysics(); }; Emit: task.desynchronize() / task.synchronize()

searchDocs.title: destructure​
searchDocs.content: </> Concurrency.destructure() → () Unpack multiple return values. Usual pairing with pcall. Syntax: auto [a, b] = expr; Emit: local a, b = expr

searchDocs.title: array​
searchDocs.content: </> Collections.array() → () Ordered list. Syntax: array<T> name = { a, b, c }; Emit: {T} array<string> names = {"Kartz", "Player1"}; for (string n in names) { post(n); } Iterate with range-for. Vector3 is a datatype, not vector<T>.

searchDocs.title: vector​
searchDocs.content: </> Collections.vector() → () Alias of array<T>. Not Vector3. Syntax: vector<T> name = { a, b }; Emit: {T}

searchDocs.title: dictionary​
searchDocs.content: </> Collections.dictionary() → () String-keyed (or typed-key) map. Access keys with :, not .. Syntax: dictionary<string, int> stats = { {"Coins", 100}, {"Gems", 50} }; post(stats:Coins); Emit: { [K]: V } with Key = value fields

searchDocs.title: iff​
searchDocs.content: control </> ControlFlow.iff() → () C-style branch. else if emits Luau elseif. Syntax: if (cond) { } else if (other) { } else { } Emit: if / elseif / else / end Parentheses required. No ternary.

searchDocs.title: while_​
searchDocs.content: control </> ControlFlow.while_() → () Loop while the condition is true. Syntax: while (cond) { } Emit: while … do … end No do/while. No continue.

searchDocs.title: c_for​
searchDocs.content: control </> ControlFlow.c_for() → () C for. Emits while plus a trailing increment. Syntax: for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { } Emit: local i = 0 / while i < n do / i += 1 Semicolons separate clauses. Range-for is a different form.

searchDocs.title: range_for​
searchDocs.content: control </> ControlFlow.range_for() → () Range-for. Prefer in. The C++-style : is the same loop, not a table key. Syntax: for (T x in list) { } · for (T x : list) { } Emit: for _, x in list do for (Player* player in players::GetPlayers()) { post(player.Name); }

searchDocs.title: guard​
searchDocs.content: control </> ControlFlow.guard() → () If the condition is false, the else block runs (usually return). Syntax: guard (condition) else { return; } Emit: if not (condition) then … end The else is required. guard (player != null) else { warn("Invalid player"); return; }

searchDocs.title: match​
searchDocs.content: control </> ControlFlow.match() → () Type switch. Instance types use IsA; primitives use typeof. _ is the fallback. Syntax: match (value) { Type name => stmt, _ => stmt }; Emit: if x:IsA("Type") then / typeof match (instance) { Part* p => p.BrickColor = BrickColor::Red(), _ => warn("unsupported") };

searchDocs.title: switch​
searchDocs.content: control </> ControlFlow.switch() → () Evaluates the discriminant once. break leaves the switch. No C fall-through; stacked cases share a body. Syntax: switch (action) { case "buy": … break; default: … break; } Emit: if / elseif inside repeat … until true

searchDocs.title: break_​
searchDocs.content: control </> ControlFlow.break_() → () Leaves the innermost loop or switch. There is no continue. Syntax: break; Emit: break

searchDocs.title: return_​
searchDocs.content: control </> ControlFlow.return_() → () Leave the current function. Syntax: return; · return expr; Emit: return / return expr

searchDocs.title: declare​
searchDocs.content: </> Functions.declare() → () Named function. Only bodies in .clp / .clpp emit. Prototypes in .clh become export type fields. Syntax: ReturnType Name(T arg) { return arg; } Emit: const function Name(arg: T): ReturnType void CreateLeaderstats(Player* player) { return; }

searchDocs.title: lambda​
searchDocs.content: </> Functions.lambda( arg: any-- Lambda parameters ) → () Closure. Empty [] only — no [x] / [&]. Luau still closes over outer locals. Syntax: func [](T arg) { } · func cb = []() {}; Emit: function(arg: T) … end players::PlayerAdded~>Connect(func [](Player* playerEntered) { post("New player: " .: playerEntered.Name); });

searchDocs.title: this​
searchDocs.content: </> Functions.this() → () The current object inside Class::Method. Emits self. Syntax: this.field · bare field → self.field There is no this->.

searchDocs.title: struct​
searchDocs.content: </> OOP.struct() → () Type declaration. class is a synonym of struct. Syntax: struct LeaderstatsServer { Janitor* janitor; }; Emit: export type plus methods; field-only headers emit const function Name() with defaults. Instances are not RAII. Leaving a block does not Destroy — use Janitor.

searchDocs.title: method​
searchDocs.content: </> OOP.method(arg: any) → () Method implementation. Syntax: void Class::Method(T arg) { this.field = arg; } Emit: function Class:Method(arg: T) Untagged files with only Class:: return the table (ModuleScript).

searchDocs.title: singleton​
searchDocs.content: </> OOP.singleton() → () Construct one service in init() and use it from lambdas. That is the game singleton. Syntax: void init() { LeaderstatsServer leaderstatsServer; }

searchDocs.title: access​
searchDocs.content: </> OOP.access() → () Parsed and ignored. Luau has no access specifiers. Syntax: public: · private: · protected: Emit: omitted

searchDocs.title: declare​
searchDocs.content: signal </> Observables.declare() → () Declare a ValueBase-backed variable. Syntax: observable T name = value; Emit: Instance.new("IntValue"); name.Value = value int → IntValue, float/double → NumberValue, string → StringValue, bool → BoolValue, else ObjectValue.

searchDocs.title: OnChange​
searchDocs.content: signal </> Observables.OnChange( handler: func-- Listener ) → () Listen to value changes. Argument is the new .Value. Syntax: name.OnChange(fn); Emit: name.Changed:Connect(fn) observable int coins = 100; coins.OnChange(func [](int newValue) { post("now " .: newValue); }); coins = 50;

searchDocs.title: include​
searchDocs.content: </> Stdlib.include() → () #include <path> / #include "path". Emit: require(…) for libs and non-stem quotes; stem quote is inlined; roblox.clh is IntelliSense only.

searchDocs.title: pragma​
searchDocs.content: </> Stdlib.pragma() → () #pragma once is valid in headers (include guard). #pragma strict emits --!strict. #pragma nostrict emits --!nonstrict. #pragma native emits --!native. #pragma optimize / #pragma optimize 2 emit --!optimize 2.

searchDocs.title: include​
searchDocs.content: </> Preprocessor.include() → () Angle-bracket includes are IntelliSense (and require for libs). Quoted sibling stem is inlined. Syntax: #include <clpp/roblox.clh> · #include "LeaderstatsServer.clh"

searchDocs.title: once​
searchDocs.content: </> Preprocessor.once() → () Include guard. Headers listed more than once are skipped. Valid at the top of every .clh. Syntax: #pragma once Emit: (none)

searchDocs.title: strict​
searchDocs.content: </> Preprocessor.strict() → () Emit --!strict at the top of the Luau file. Syntax: #pragma strict Emit: --!strict

searchDocs.title: nostrict​
searchDocs.content: </> Preprocessor.nostrict() → () Emit --!nonstrict. Aliases: nstrict, nonstrict. Syntax: #pragma nostrict Emit: --!nonstrict

searchDocs.title: native​
searchDocs.content: </> Preprocessor.native() → () Emit --!native (Luau native codegen). Syntax: #pragma native Emit: --!native

searchDocs.title: optimize​
searchDocs.content: </> Preprocessor.optimize() → () Emit --!optimize N. Bare optimize means 2. Syntax: #pragma optimize · #pragma optimize 2 · #pragma optimize 1 · #pragma optimize 0 Emit: --!optimize 2

searchDocs.title: method_scope​
searchDocs.content: operator </> Operators.method_scope() → () Method call and nested name. Syntax: obj::Method(args); · obj::Child (no call) · Class::Method (definition) Emit: obj:Method(args) / obj.Child players::PlayerAdded::Connect(fn); player::FindFirstChild("x"); Datatype / task::wait emit . (not Instance methods).

searchDocs.title: table_key​
searchDocs.content: operator </> Operators.table_key() → () Dictionary / module table key. Not a method call. Syntax: Table:Key Emit: Table.Key DataService:Server::WaitFor(p); post(stats:Coins); Range-for uses in (or :) in a different position: for (T x in list).

searchDocs.title: property​
searchDocs.content: operator </> Operators.property() → () Instance or value property. Syntax: instance.Property Emit: instance.Property player.Name = "Kartz";

searchDocs.title: concat​
searchDocs.content: operator </> Operators.concat() → () String concatenation. Never + or Lua ... Syntax: a .: b .: c Emit: a .. b (left-associative) return player.Name .: "_LeaderstatsJanitor";

searchDocs.title: janitor_connect​
searchDocs.content: operator </> Operators.janitor_connect( fn: func-- Listener ) → () Subscribe and give the connection to Janitor. ~>Connect and ~>Once only. Syntax: signal~>Connect(fn); · signal~>Once(fn); Emit: janitor:Add(signal:Connect(fn), "Disconnect") Looks up janitor local, self.janitor, or synthetic __janitor.

searchDocs.title: arithmetic​
searchDocs.content: operator </> Operators.arithmetic() → () Numeric arithmetic. + does not concatenate. * is never pointer deref. Syntax: a + b - c * d / e Emit: same operators

searchDocs.title: comparison​
searchDocs.content: operator </> Operators.comparison() → () != emits ~=. The others stay the same. Syntax: a != b · a == b Emit: ~= / == / < / > / <= / >=

searchDocs.title: logic​
searchDocs.content: operator </> Operators.logic() → () Boolean logic. Syntax: a && b || !c Emit: and / or / not No ternary ? :.

searchDocs.title: assignment​
searchDocs.content: operator </> Operators.assignment() → () Assignment and compound assignment. Syntax: name = value; · name += 1; Emit: = += -= *= /= Observable assignment writes .Value.

searchDocs.title: increment​
searchDocs.content: operator </> Operators.increment() → () Always emits += 1 / -= 1. Prefix/postfix value is not preserved. Syntax: i++; · i--;

searchDocs.title: designated​
searchDocs.content: operator </> Operators.designated() → () C++ designated initializer → Luau table field. Syntax: Type { .Field = value } Emit: { Field = value }

searchDocs.title: signal​
searchDocs.content: signal </> Signals.signal() → () Declare a typed signal. Syntax: signal<Player*, int> OnCoinsUpdated; Emit: local OnCoinsUpdated = __signal()

searchDocs.title: Fire​
searchDocs.content: signal </> Signals.Fire( ...: any-- Payload matching signal<T...> ) → () Emits to every current listener. Syntax: name::Fire(...); Emit: name:Fire(...) signal<Player*, int> OnCoinsUpdated; OnCoinsUpdated::Fire(player, 500);

searchDocs.title: Connect​
searchDocs.content: signal </> Signals.Connect( handler: func-- Listener ) → () Subscribe until Disconnect. Prefer ~>Connect so Janitor owns the connection. Syntax: name::Connect(fn); · name~>Connect(fn); Emit: name:Connect(fn) or janitor:Add(..., "Disconnect")

searchDocs.title: Once​
searchDocs.content: signal </> Signals.Once( handler: func-- Listener ) → () Subscribe for a single emission, then disconnect. ~>Once is janitor-managed. Syntax: name::Once(fn); · name~>Once(fn); Emit: name:Once(fn)

searchDocs.title: Wait​
searchDocs.content: signal </> Signals.Wait() → () Yields until the next Fire. Syntax: name::Wait(); Emit: name:Wait()

searchDocs.title: GetPropertyChangedSignal​
searchDocs.content: signal </> Signals.GetPropertyChangedSignal( name: string-- Property name ) → () Engine signal for one Instance property. Syntax: obj::GetPropertyChangedSignal("Name")~>Connect(fn); Emit: obj:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Name")

searchDocs.title: Patterns​
searchDocs.content: Tool	Useoptional<T>	missing enchant, missing Instance array<T>	hotbar slots dictionary<K,V>	id → count func	first-class predicates static_cast<T>	annotate after FindFirstChild Player* vs Instance*	match narrows with IsA signal<Player*, ItemStack>	typed economy events observable int	HUD-facing counts

searchDocs.title: Signal of structs​
searchDocs.content: signal<Player*, ItemStack> OnGrant; OnGrant~>Connect(func [](Player* player, ItemStack stack) { guard (stack.Count > 0) else { return; } post(player.Name .: " got " .: stack.Id); }); OnGrant::Fire(player, ItemStack { .Id = "gem", .Count = 3 });   Designated initializers fill the struct/table in one expression.

searchDocs.title: What is still not C++​
searchDocs.content: No templates beyond the mapped ones (array, dictionary, GetService, static_cast, optional, signal). No overloading. No std::vector methods — you emit Luau tables and use table / your own helpers.  Next: Advanced production patterns.

searchDocs.title: Why this is “production-shaped”​
searchDocs.content: guard keeps every callback flat.match is the Instance type switch you would write with a pile of IsA in Luau.Once on Touched so a pickup cannot fire twice.observable combo is HUD-ready (combo.OnChange on the client).signal::Fire decouples damage from UI.[[server]] documents that workspace watching is not a LocalScript concern.~> means you do not leak connections when the janitor cleans up.  Full file: examples/advanced/CombatServer.server.clpp.  Next: Cheat sheet.

searchDocs.title: int​
searchDocs.content: type </> Types.int() → () IEEE-looking integer in source. Luau numbers are doubles. Syntax: int name = 0; Emit: number observable int → IntValue. Always initialize: int coins; emits nil.

searchDocs.title: float​
searchDocs.content: type </> Types.float() → () Floating-point number. Same emit as int and double. Syntax: float speed = 16.5; Emit: number observable float → NumberValue.

searchDocs.title: double​
searchDocs.content: type </> Types.double() → () Same emit as float. Syntax: double alpha = 0.25; Emit: number

searchDocs.title: bool​
searchDocs.content: type </> Types.bool() → () Boolean. Literals true / false. ! emits not. Syntax: bool isActive = true; Emit: boolean

searchDocs.title: string​
searchDocs.content: type </> Types.string() → () UTF-8 text. Not std::string. Concatenate with .:. Double quotes, single quotes, and template strings with {expr}. Syntax: string name = "Kartz"; Emit: string

searchDocs.title: void​
searchDocs.content: type </> Types.void() → () No value. Return type of procedures. void init() is the script entry. Syntax: void Name(T arg) { return; } Emit: no return annotation

searchDocs.title: func​
searchDocs.content: type </> Types.func() → () Function type and optional lambda prefix. Syntax: func cb = [](int n) { }; Emit: (...any) -> any

searchDocs.title: auto​
searchDocs.content: type </> Types.auto() → () Infer the type from the initializer. Syntax: auto* players = GetService<Players>(); Inferred for new, GetService<T>(), datatype constructors, and destructuring.

searchDocs.title: optional​
searchDocs.content: type </> Types.optional() → () A value that may be missing. Syntax: optional<T> name = null; Emit: T?

searchDocs.title: instance_pointer​
searchDocs.content: type </> Types.instance_pointer() → () Player* means an Instance of class Player — not a heap pointer. Syntax: Player* player = null; Emit: star stripped (Player) Properties use .. Methods use ::. No delete, *p, &p, int&, or ->.

searchDocs.title: const​
searchDocs.content: type </> Types.const() → () const / static constexpr become Luau const. Syntax: const int DoubleCoins(int coins) { return coins; } Emit: const function

searchDocs.title: static_cast​
searchDocs.content: type </> Types.static_cast(x: any) → () Source-level cast. Does not check ClassName. Syntax: T static_cast<T>(x); Emit: x

searchDocs.title: Goals​
searchDocs.content: Write like C++ (types, struct, new, GetService<T>), with our own operators: :: method/scope, : table, . property, .: concatenation.Emit modern Luau (local, const, const function, Instance.new, game:GetService).One input file becomes one output file (Rojo infers Script / LocalScript / ModuleScript from the name).Own extensions: .clh, .clp, .clpp — not .h / .cpp.

searchDocs.title: What we are not​
searchDocs.content: CL++ is not a full C++ compiler and not the Roblox API connector. There is no std::, pointer arithmetic, delete, overloading, generic templates (beyond the mapped ones), continue, ternary, do/while, try/catch, or goto.  Player* is not a heap address: it is a Roblox Instance of class Player. Access is player.Name / player::FindFirstChild(...), not ->.  Range-for uses : between the name and the collection: for (Player* player : players::GetPlayers()). Table : (DataService:Server) lives in expressions, not in a C-style for header (for (int i = 0; ...)).

searchDocs.title: guard — fail fast​
searchDocs.content: If the condition is false, the else block runs. Almost always you return (or report).  void LeaderstatsServer::PlayerEntered(Player* player) { guard (player != null) else { warn("Invalid player"); return; } guard (player.Parent != null) else { return; } post(player.Name); }   if not (player ~= nil) then warn("Invalid player") return end   Use guard at the top of methods. Happy-path code stays unindented.

searchDocs.title: match — types and values​
searchDocs.content: match (instance) { Part* p => p.Anchored = true, Model* m => post(m.Name), string s => post(s), _ => warn("Instance not supported") };   Part* p → x:IsA("Part") then bind p.string s → typeof(x) == "string"._ is required as a fallback in real UI code so unknown instances do not silently drop.  Arms can be a block:  match (tool) { Tool* t => { guard (t.Parent != null) else { return; } t::Activate(); }, _ => warn("not a tool") };   Next: Async, spawn, parallel.

searchDocs.title: if​
searchDocs.content: if (coins > 50) { post("Enough balance!"); } else if (coins == 0) { warn("No coins!"); } else { report("Balance sync error."); }   else if emits elseif.

searchDocs.title: while and for​
searchDocs.content: while (true) { post("tick"); } for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) { post("Count: " .: i); } for (Player* player in players::GetPlayers()) { post("Player connected: " .: player.Name); }   C-for counts. Range-for uses in (or :) to name the collection.

searchDocs.title: switch​
searchDocs.content: Evaluates the discriminant once. Stacked cases share a body. break leaves the switch. No C fall-through.  switch (action) { case "buy": case "purchase": Grant(player); break; default: warn("unknown"); break; }

searchDocs.title: 3. Pointers are Instances​
searchDocs.content: Player* is a Roblox Player. There is no delete, no *player, no player->Name. Lifetime is Destroy or Janitor.

searchDocs.title: 4. init starts a script; modules return tables​
searchDocs.content: Scripts: define void init(). Modules: usually do not define init() unless the require should run it.

searchDocs.title: 5. CL++ is the language; Cluaupp is the engine cable​
searchDocs.content: If a Roblox class is missing from IntelliSense, that is a Cluaupp generated-header problem, not a CL++ syntax problem.

searchDocs.content: I/O — post, warn, report CL++	Luau	Usepost(...)	print(...)	normal output warn(...)	warn(...)	recoverable problems report(...)	error(...)	stop the thread post("ok"); warn("careful"); report("failed"); Legacy C++ streams still parse: cout << "hi" << endl — each << is another argument, endl ends the line. searchDocs.content: If the file defines void init(), emit places init() at the end of Scripts and LocalScripts. There is no int main().  Shared modules must not define init() unless they should run on require.

searchDocs.title: Grammar (subset)
searchDocs.content: Grammar (subset) EBNF of the slice the lexer/parser must accept. This is not ISO C++. translation-unit = { include | pragma | using-skip | declaration } ; include = "#include" ( "<" path ">" | '"' path '"' ) ; pragma = "#pragma" ( "once" | "strict" | "nostrict" | "nstrict" | "nonstrict" | "native" | "optimize" [ 0 | 1 | 2 ] ) ; declaration = struct-decl | function-def | method-def | var-decl | const-decl ; struct-decl = ( "struct" | "class" ) ident "{" { struct-member } "}" ";" ; struct-member = access-label | "static" "constexpr" type ident "=" expr ";" | type ident [ "=" expr ] ";" | type ident "(" [ param-list ] ")" ";" ; function-def = type ident "(" [ param-list ] ")" block ; method-def = type ident "::" ident "(" [ param-list ] ")" block ; param-list = param { "," param } ; param = type ident ; type = "void" | "int" | "float" | "double" | "bool" | "string" | "func" | "auto" | ident [ "*" ] | ( "LuaArray" | "vector" | "array" | "span" | "optional" ) "<" type ">" | "dictionary" "<" type "," type ">" | "const" type ; block = "{" { statement } "}" ; statement = var-decl | expr ";" | "return" [ expr ] ";" | "break" ";" | if-stmt | while-stmt | c-for | range-for | spawn-stmt | parallel-stmt | guard-stmt | match-stmt | switch-stmt | destructure | block ; guard-stmt = "guard" "(" expr ")" "else" statement ; spawn-stmt = "spawn" block [ ";" ] ; parallel-stmt = "parallel" block [ ";" ] ; match-stmt = "match" "(" expr ")" "{" { match-arm } "}" [ ";" ] ; match-arm = ( "_" | type ident ) "=>" ( block | expr ) [ "," ] ; destructure = "auto" "[" ident { "," ident } "]" "=" expr ";" ; if-stmt = "if" "(" expr ")" statement [ "else" statement ] ; while-stmt = "while" "(" expr ")" statement ; c-for = "for" "(" [ var-init ] ";" [ expr ] ";" [ expr ] ")" statement ; range-for = "for" "(" type ident ":" expr ")" statement ; switch-stmt = "switch" "(" expr ")" "{" { case-clause } "}" ; case-clause = ( "case" expr | "default" ) ":" { statement } ; expr = ident | number | string | "true" | "false" | "null" | expr ( "+" | "-" | "*" | "/" | "==" | "!=" | "<" | ">" | "<=" | ">=" | "&&" | "||" | ".:" ) expr | "!" expr | "-" expr | expr ( "=" | "+=" | "-=" | "*=" | "/=" ) expr | expr "++" | expr "--" | expr "::" ident [ "(" arg-list ")" ] | expr ":" ident [ "(" arg-list ")" ] | expr "." ident [ "(" arg-list ")" ] | ident "(" arg-list ")" | "new" ident "(" [ arg-list ] ")" | "GetService" "<" ident ">" "(" ")" | "static_cast" "<" type ">" "(" expr ")" | ident "{" { "." ident "=" expr "," } "}" | "{" expr { "," expr } "}" | "{" "{" expr "," expr "}" { "," "{" expr "," expr "}" } "}" | lambda | "(" expr ")" ; lambda = [ "func" ] "[]" [ "(" [ param-list ] ")" ] block ; Concatenation uses .: (not ..). :: is method/scope; : is table; . is property. Extra mapped tokens, not pure grammar: string_concat, cout, cerr, endl, post, warn, report.

searchDocs.title: Pointers are Instances​
searchDocs.content: Player* means “an Instance of class Player”. Properties use .. Methods use ::.  player.Name = "Kartz"; player::FindFirstChild("leaderstats");   player.Name = "Kartz" player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats")   There is no pointer arithmetic and no std::unique_ptr. Lifetime is Roblox's: Destroy or Janitor.

searchDocs.content: Inferred when the value is new Class(...), GetService<T>(), or a datatype constructor. Prefer an explicit type on parameters and struct fields.

searchDocs.content: static_cast<T>(x), const_cast, reinterpret_cast, and dynamic_cast emit the argument. (void)x; disappears (silences unused in clangd). Luau has no casts — they do not check ClassName.

searchDocs.title: Counter​
searchDocs.content: #include <clpp/roblox.clh> void init() { Players* players = GetService<Players>(); Player* localPlayer = players.LocalPlayer; guard (localPlayer != null) else { return; } PlayerGui* playerGui = localPlayer::WaitForChild("PlayerGui"); auto create = Vide:create; auto source = Vide:source; auto apply = Vide:apply; auto count = source(0); auto makeGui = create("ScreenGui"); auto makeButton = create("TextButton"); auto makeLabel = create("TextLabel"); auto label = makeLabel({ {"BackgroundTransparency", 1}, {"Size", UDim2.fromScale(1, 0.5)}, {"TextColor3", Color3.fromRGB(240, 240, 255)}, {"Text", func []() { return "Clicks: " .: count(); }} }); auto button = makeButton({ {"Size", UDim2.fromScale(1, 0.5)}, {"Position", UDim2.fromScale(0, 0.5)}, {"Text", "Once-safe click"}, {"Activated", func []() { count(count() + 1); }} }); auto gui = makeGui({ {"Name", "VideCounter"}, {"ResetOnSpawn", false}, {"Parent", playerGui} }); auto mount = apply(gui); mount({ label, button }); }   Vide Text can be a function. CL++ lambdas func []() { return ...; } become that function. Vide re-runs it when count() changes.

searchDocs.title: Vide + CL++ Once​
searchDocs.content: If a Roblox event should update UI once (tutorial toast):  workspace.ChildAdded~>Once(func [](Instance* child) { match (child) { BasePart* p => count(count() + 1), _ => warn("ignored") }; });   ~> still uses Janitor. Vide sources stay independent of that connection.  Full file: examples/ui/VideCounter.client.clpp.  Next: Advanced typing.

searchDocs.title: Mental model​
searchDocs.content: Create a scope (owns all state and instances; destroy the scope to clean up).Put numbers/strings you care about in Value.New(scope, "ClassName") returns a constructor. Call it with a dictionary of properties.Nested instances go under the Fusion Children key — a dictionary pair {Children, child}.

searchDocs.title: Events and cleanup​
searchDocs.content: Fusion's OnEvent is a table key, just like Children:  auto OnEvent = Fusion:OnEvent; auto newButton = Fusion:New(scope, "TextButton"); newButton({ {"Text", "+10"}, {OnEvent("Activated"), func []() { coins(coins() + 10); }} });   When the scope is destroyed, Fusion destroys instances and disconnects. You still use CL++ ~> for engine signals outside Fusion (PlayerAdded, DataService).

searchDocs.title: Pattern with guard + match​
searchDocs.content: Drive the same HUD from inventory instances:  void BindDrop(Instance* inst, auto coins) { match (inst) { IntValue* v => { guard (v.Name == "Coins") else { return; } coins(v.Value); v.OnChange(func [](int n) { coins(n); }); }, _ => warn("not a coins value") }; }   Full file: examples/ui/FusionHud.client.clpp.  Next: Vide.

searchDocs.title: Where a name lives​
searchDocs.content: File-level declarations → file local / const.Inside a function → from that line to the end of the block. Nested { } may shadow.Inside Class::Method → this is self. Bare field names become self.field. Parameters shadow fields.

searchDocs.title: Globals that stay bare​
searchDocs.content: post, warn, report, game, workspace, task, library types, Instance classes, datatypes.

searchDocs.title: Lifetime​
searchDocs.content: Leaving a { } block does not Destroy Instances. Use Janitor, ~>Connect, or an explicit ::Destroy().

searchDocs.title: Destructuring​
searchDocs.content: auto [ok, result] = pcall(func []() { return 1; });   Emits local ok, result = pcall(...).  Next: Functions and lambdas.

searchDocs.title: What CL++ does not do
searchDocs.content: What CL++ does not do CL++ is a subset. If you reach for these, rewrite the idea in Luau terms. Full ISO C++ (templates, overloading, RAII delete, std::)->, int&, pointer arithmetic, *partcontinue, ternary ? :, do/while, try/catch, gotoC++ lambda captures [x], [&]JSXMacros other than #pragma once / strict / nostrict / native / optimizeConnecting Roblox APIs for you — that is Cluaupp The compiler will either skip the construct (using, namespace, enum declarations) or fail to parse. Prefer the cheat sheet surface.

searchDocs.title: Functions​
searchDocs.content: void CreateLeaderstats(Player* player) { return; } const int DoubleCoins(int coins) { return coins; }   const function CreateLeaderstats(player: Player) return end const function DoubleCoins(coins: number): number return coins end   Only functions with a body emit from a .clp / .clpp. Prototypes in a .clh become export type fields.No overloading — one name, one emit. No default arguments.void init() at the end of Script / LocalScript. There is no int main().

searchDocs.title: Scopes​
searchDocs.content: File-level declarations become file local / const.Function declarations last from that line to the end of the block. Nested { } may shadow.In Class::Method, this is self. Bare fields become self.field. Calls to other methods become self:Method(...). Parameters and locals shadow fields.Globals stay bare: post, warn, report, game, workspace, lib types, Instances, datatypes.Instances are not RAII. Leaving a block does not Destroy — use Janitor.

searchDocs.title: Control flow​
searchDocs.content: if (coins > 50) { post("Enough balance!"); } else if (coins == 0) { warn("No coins!"); } else { report("Balance sync error."); } while (true) { post("tick"); } for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) { post("Count: " .: i); } for (Player* player : players::GetPlayers()) { post("Player connected: " .: player.Name); } switch (action) { case "buy": case "purchase": Grant(player); break; case "sell": if (amount <= 0) { break; } Take(player); break; default: warn("unknown"); break; }   if coins > 50 then print("Enough balance!") elseif coins == 0 then warn("No coins!") else error("Balance sync error.") end while true do print("tick") end local i = 0 while i < 10 do print("Count: " .. i) i += 1 end for _, player in players:GetPlayers() do print("Player connected: " .. player.Name) end   switch evaluates the discriminant once, then becomes if / elseif / else inside repeat … until true so break still leaves the switch. Stacked cases share the body. No C-style fall-through.  else if emits Luau elseif. Range-for: for (Type name : list). C loop: for (int i = 0; i < n; i++). Unsupported: continue, do/while, ternary, ->.

searchDocs.title: Expressions and operators​
searchDocs.content: CL++	Luaunull	nil true / false	true / false !=	~= &&	and ||	or !	not == + - * / < > <= >=	same (* is multiply; + only adds numbers) "text"	"text" = += -= *= /=	same ++ / --	+= 1 / -= 1 obj.Prop	obj.Prop DataService:Server	DataService.Server obj::Method(a)	obj:Method(a) a .: b	a .. b fn(a)	fn(a) Type { .Field = value }	{ Field = value } unary -	-  Binary operators associate left-to-right — use parentheses when mixing.  Designated initializers become Luau tables:  DataService:Server::Init(DataServiceOptions { .Template = playerData, .StoreName = "PlayerData", .UseMock = true, });   DataService.Server:Init({ Template = playerData, StoreName = "PlayerData", UseMock = true, })

searchDocs.title: Strings​
searchDocs.content: Concatenation is the .: operator. It emits Luau ... Do not write .. or use + to join text.  a .: b .: c associates left-to-right: (a .. b) .. cstring_concat(a, b, c) remains valid: zero args → "", one arg → the value, several → (a .. b .. c)  return player.Name .: "_LeaderstatsJanitor"; return player.Name .: "_" .: "LeaderstatsJanitor"; return string_concat(player.Name, "_", "LeaderstatsJanitor");   return player.Name .. "_LeaderstatsJanitor" return (player.Name .. "_") .. "LeaderstatsJanitor" return (player.Name .. "_" .. "LeaderstatsJanitor")

searchDocs.title: post / warn / report​
searchDocs.content: CL++	Luaupost(...)	print(...) warn(...)	warn(...) report(...)	error(...)  cout << … << endl remains valid (C++ legacy): each << is another argument, endl ends the line.  post("ok"); warn("careful"); report("failed");   print("ok") warn("careful") error("failed")

searchDocs.title: new and services​
searchDocs.content: auto* coins = new IntValue(leaderstats); auto* players = GetService<Players>(); auto* janitor = new Janitor(); part.Size = Vector3(8, 1, 8); part.CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(from, look); part.Material = Enum.Material.Plastic;   local coins: IntValue = Instance.new("IntValue") coins.Parent = leaderstats local players: Players = game:GetService("Players") local janitor = Janitor.new() part.Size = Vector3.new(8, 1, 8) part.CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(from, look) part.Material = Enum.Material.Plastic   The first argument of new Class(parent) becomes .Parent on Instance classes. Libs use Janitor.new(). Datatypes use Vector3(...), not new.

searchDocs.title: Callbacks (events and lambdas)​
searchDocs.content: Lambdas use empty [] (no C++ captures). func is the type and may prefix the lambda. Luau closures capture the environment; keep Instances alive with Janitor.  func onCoinsChanged = [](int newValue) { post("New value: " .: newValue); }; players::PlayerAdded::Connect(func [](Player* playerEntered) { post("New player: " .: playerEntered.Name); }); game::BindToClose(func []() { janitor::Cleanup(); });   Passing a method by name from inside Class:: binds self: function(...) self:OnPlayer(...) end.

searchDocs.title: Collections​
searchDocs.content: array<string> names = {"Kartz", "Player1"}; dictionary<string, int> stats = { {"Coins", 100}, {"Gems", 50} };   local names: {string} = { "Kartz", "Player1" } local stats: { [string]: number } = { Coins = 100, Gems = 50 }

searchDocs.title: OOP: structs, methods, singletons​
searchDocs.content: The type lives in a struct (or class) in the sibling .clh. Methods are Class::Method in the .clp / .clpp. void init() starts the script.  static constexpr becomes const.Fields are self.field. public: / private: are ignored.Nested structs with defaults become nested tables (DataService Templates). array<T> / LuaArray<T> fields stay on the table.Class:: emits function Class:Method(...).Construct one service in init() (LeaderstatsServer leaderstatsServer;) and use it in lambdas. That is the game singleton.Lib singletons: DataService:Server / DataService:Client.Field-only structs in the header emit const function Name() with defaults.Untagged files with only Class:: return the table (ModuleScript).  Stems must match: LeaderstatsServer.clh next to LeaderstatsServer.server.clpp.

searchDocs.title: :: vs : vs . vs .:​
searchDocs.content: CL++ does not use ->. Methods and scope use ::. Tables/dictionaries use :. Instance properties use .. Concatenation is .:.  CL++	Luau	Whenplayers::PlayerAdded::Connect(fn)	players.PlayerAdded:Connect(fn)	method / signal player::FindFirstChild("x")	player:FindFirstChild("x")	Instance method janitor::Add(conn)	janitor:Add(conn)	lib method DataService:Server	DataService.Server	table key DataService:Server::WaitFor(p)	DataService.Server:WaitFor(p)	table + method player.Name	player.Name	property a .: b	a .. b	concatenation for (T x in list)	for _, x in list do	range-for (: still works) for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)	while + i += 1	C loop signal~>Connect(fn)	janitor:Add(signal:Connect(fn), "Disconnect")	auto-cleanup signal~>Once(fn)	janitor:Add(signal:Once(fn), "Disconnect")	one-shot auto-cleanup signal::Fire(...)	signal:Fire(...)	emit / send obj::GetPropertyChangedSignal("Name")	obj:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Name")	property change signal

searchDocs.title: observable​
searchDocs.content: observable T name = value becomes a ValueBase. Reads/writes use .Value. OnChange listens to Changed.  observable int coins = 100; coins.OnChange(func [](int newValue) { post("Coins changed to: " .: newValue); }); coins = 50; post(coins);   local coins: IntValue = Instance.new("IntValue") coins.Value = 100 coins.Changed:Connect(function(newValue: number) print("Coins changed to: " .. newValue) end) coins.Value = 50 print(coins.Value)   int → IntValue, float/double → NumberValue, string → StringValue, bool → BoolValue, everything else → ObjectValue.

searchDocs.title: guard​
searchDocs.content: guard (player != null) else { warn("Invalid player"); return; } post(player.Name);   if not (player ~= nil) then warn("Invalid player") return end print(player.Name)

searchDocs.title: Auto-cleanup ~>​
searchDocs.content: signal~>Connect(fn) and signal~>Once(fn) register the connection on the scope Janitor (janitor local, self.janitor, or a synthetic __janitor). Once disconnects after the first emission. In void init(), the synthetic __janitor also gets game:BindToClose.  players::PlayerAdded~>Connect(func [](Player* player) { post("Connected and managed automatically!"); }); players::PlayerAdded~>Once(func [](Player* player) { post("First player only"); });   janitor:Add(players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player: Player) print("Connected and managed automatically!") end), "Disconnect") janitor:Add(players.PlayerAdded:Once(function(player: Player) print("First player only") end), "Disconnect")

": " .. newAmount) end), "Disconnect") janitor:Add(OnCoinsUpdated:Once(function(player: Player, newAmount: number) print("first: " .. newAmount) end), "Disconnect") OnCoinsUpdated:Fire(player, 500) part:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Transparency"):Connect(function() print(part.Transparency) end)   CL++	Meaningsignal<T...> name;	typed signal (BindableEvent under __signal()) name::Fire(...)	send the signal name~>Connect(fn)	listen until disconnected (Janitor) name~>Once(fn)	listen once, then disconnect name::Wait()	yield until the next fire assign an observable	writes .Value and fires Changed obj::GetPropertyChangedSignal("X")	Instance property change signal
